tn_quiet_zone_the.blurb: The Quiet Zone is the far-right stretch of the limestone bluff above the Cumberland River at King's Bluff in Clarksville. It holds 25 routes, mostly bolted with a handful of trad lines, on short walls of small edges and pockets. Grades centre on 5.9 through 5.11, with a few easier lines in the 5.5 to 5.8 range and a single 5.12. Because the harder lines dominate, it tends to be calmer than the rest of the bluff. The walk from the parking area is only a few minutes via the stairs and a turn to the right. Good for confident leaders who want steady 5.10s.

tn_lonesome_wall.blurb: Lonesome Wall is the section of King's Bluff, the limestone cliff over the Cumberland River in Clarksville, where the steeper and harder bolted lines live. Of its 24 routes, nearly all are sport. The spread is wide: a couple of easy warm-ups, a solid middle of 5.8 to 5.10, then a good number of 5.11s and several 5.12s, making it the place to head when you want a real test. The approach is a quick stroll from the parking area, down the stairs and then right along the base. Expect short, technical face climbing on edges and pockets.

tn_alley_the.blurb: The Alley is a compact corner of King's Bluff, the Clarksville limestone crag above the Cumberland River. Its 24 climbs are short and nearly all bolted, with a couple of trad lines and one low traverse problem. Most sit between 5.4 and 5.9, which makes it one of the friendlier spots for newer leaders, though a few 5.11s add something for stronger climbers. Bolts are placed close together to suit the modest height. Find it by following the stairs down and heading right; a chest-high ledge and a small boulder seat mark the middle of the wall.

tn_black_stacks.blurb: Black Stacks is a shaded, creekside cliff in Rocky Fork State Park near Erwin in the Unicoi County hills of east Tennessee. Climbing here is mainly traditional: about 23 of its 25 routes need gear, with two bolted lines. Most grades fall at 5.9 and 5.10, with a few easier routes and one 5.11, and the cracks are moderate with varied, enjoyable movement. It sees very little sun, so it suits hot days, though the lower part of the wall can stay wet after rain. Reaching it involves a walk on gravel trail and a creek crossing on a fallen tree.
